title: steadyflow-release-ops-weekly-planner-and-rollback-cheat-sheet-2026
summary: Compact, tactical weekly planner for an incremental release with a short rollback cheat-sheet and a terse release-notes draft. Focus: minimize customer-facing churn, keep latency SLOs stable, and make rollbacks deterministic.
body:
Purpose:
- Practical week-of-release planner for small-to-medium rollouts (staged region + capacity burst).
- Lightweight ops cadence + decision triggers, quick rollback checklist, and a one-paragraph release notes draft for SEC/CS handoff.

High-level constraints and assumptions:
- Target release window: weekday early-morning rollout (region TZ local 03:00-07:00) to reduce peak impact.
- Canary population: 2% traffic for first 30 minutes, 10% after 2 hours, 50% at 8 hours, full at 24 hours — unless metrics fail.
- SLOs: 99th p50 latency < 180ms, error rate < 0.1% for generation endpoints.
- Monitoring: token-level cost, tail latency, error taxonomy (502/timeout/decoder-fail), and model-quality regressions (eval-triggered).

Weekly planner (day-by-day, minimal ops language):
- 3 business days before (D-3):
  - Owner: release lead (Rina) — lock PR list, freeze non-critical infra changes.
  - Verify canary infra is green: autoscaler, prefix cache warmers, and KV cache replication health.
  - Prep telemetry dashboards: baseline and comparison cohorts. Add alert thresholds to pager duty.
  - TODO: coordinate with CS for briefing note (quick bulleted list).

- 1 business day before (D-1):
  - Owner: SRE oncall (Tomás) — run a rehearsal dry-run in staging: smoke long-tail token loads, send synthetic requests matching top 10 customer prompt patterns.
  - Evaluate capacity plan against expected QPS spike + 30% buffer.
  - Confirm rollback image/build exists and is tagged in registry.
  - Send release calendar invite + Slack #release-ops ping with short runbook link.

- Day-of (D):
  - T-3h: quick preflight sync (15m): release lead, SRE, platform, and product coverage. Confirm monitoring hooks.
  - T-1h: take a final snapshot of key dashboards and save a shortscreen. Post to the runbook.
  - T+0: update traffic router: route canary to new variant (2%).
  - T+10m: sanity check – API heartbeats, basic smoke tests, model decode sanity.
  - T+30m: metrics snapshot and compare to baseline. If >1.5x baseline tail latency or >2x error rate -> rollback (see triggers below).
  - T+2h: if stable, increase to 10% and re-evaluate after 30m.
  - T+8h: soft-open to 50% if all gates pass.
  - T+24h: full release unless an active mitigation is in place.

Observation windows and who watches when (shift-friendly):
- 0–4h: primary SRE + release lead watching on-call channel; product signals (regressions) routed to product owner.
- 4–12h: SRE rotated in; telemetry SME (Diego) reviews model-quality alerts.
- 12–24h: operations handoff to next-day SRE; keep an inline timeline with decisions and screenshots.

Quick decision triggers (go / hold / rollback):
- Immediate rollback (act now) if any of the following during canary or early ramp:
  - HTTP 5xx error rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m AND user-visible errors increase.
  - P50 latency jumps > 2x baseline and p99 > 300ms 3 consecutive samples (5m sample cadence).
  - Model quality degradation: auto-eval regression > threshold (see linked eval job id in artifacts).
- Hold and debug (pause ramp) if:
  - Memory or GPU OOMs observed on >1 host or transiently across 10% of hosts.
  - Data-plane errors with unclear root-cause.
- Continue if:
  - All major metrics within 15% of baseline and no new error classes show up.

Rollback cheat-sheet (short, copyable):
- Who: SRE oncall executes rollback, release lead coordinates comms, platform team runs the image swap.
- Steps (5-minute core path):
  1) Post to #release-ops: "ROLLBACK STARTING — reason: <short reason>" and ping PD.
  2) Traffic router: switch traffic back to previous stable model tag (registry tag: stable-<date>-<build>).
  3) Verify: quick smoke (health endpoints + 10 representative prompts).
  4) Revert infra changes (if any) via ops rollback: terraform apply with previous plan or use stored infra snapshot.
  5) Mark incident ticket: JIRA-ENG-xxxx and add timeline notes.
  6) Post-mortem: schedule within 48 hours; capture timeline + resource utilization + debounce plan.

Post-rollback checklist (short):
- Confirm customer-facing errors reduced to baseline within 15 minutes.
- Disable any temporary mitigations that were toggled.
- Export telemetry snapshots and attach to incident.
- Quick sync with product to decide if reattempt should be delayed or reworked.

Smoke and validation matrix (minimal):
- Health (automated): /health, model-liveness, queue-depth < 20.
- Smoke (synthetic): 10 prompt types across short/long context, include edge tokenization cases.
- Load: 1.5x typical canary QPS for 5 minutes.
- Quality: run lightweight eval set (50 prompts) and compare top-1 scoring buckets.

Telemetry and alerts to enable for week-of release (must exist before T-1h):
- p50/p95/p99 latency for generation endpoints (tag by model variant).
- Error taxonomy: 4xx vs 5xx vs decoder/transformer fails.
- Token throughput and cost-per-token delta.
- Model-eval regression alerts (auto-run job id in linked_artifacts).
- Autoscaler oscillation detector (flapping > 3 scaling events in 10m).

Runbook annex: short templates and snippets to copy into incident notes
- Release announcement (to CS/ops):
  Subject: Release rolling out — <short name> — canary @ 2% now
  Body: Quick summary, owners, expected impact, rollback triggers, channel to watch (#release-ops).

- Post-release one-paragraph notes (for release notes draft):
  "Production rollout of <feature-name> (build <build-id>) — incremental staged deployment across regions. This change improves model prompt-routing and reduces median latency for multi-turn prompts. If you observe increased latency or errors, please contact support@redwood.com and reference JIRA-ENG-2142."

Unresolved questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Confirm if the canary percentage cadence should be shortened for EU region (customer base is more bursty).
- Add a preflight checklist item for KMS key rotation impacts (security asked for a pointer).
- Finalize the exact eval threshold numbers with applied-ml team (Diego).

Appendix: quick links and snippets
- Quick CLI: router set-variant --target new --percent 2 --region us-west-2
- Smoke commands: scripts/smoke/run_smoke.sh --suite quick10
- Regenerate rollback tag: registry.redwood/internal/model/stable-20260909:sha256-abc123

Notes on doc style: keep this intentionally terse — it's an ops sandwich sheet for a small team launch. Add more automation later (runbook-run requests).

Last edited by: Aisha Kapoor (2026-09-12)
review_notes: Drafted from previous ops experience. Needs sign-off from applied-ml for eval thresholds and from CS for the customer-facing paragraph before finalizing.
